chapter_intro: Volume I is the reusable foundation layer for the Lean formalization. Later volumes should import these declarations instead of recreating generic equality, set, function, relation, operation, order, or algebra laws.

The most important design rule is to prove generic mathematics once against an interface, then provide concrete adapters for each backend. For sets, ordinary set-theory proofs should target SetInterface and SetInterfaceLaws, while implementation files prove that a concrete backend satisfies those laws.

volume_map.purpose: formal languages, syntax, semantics, proof systems, models, and model comparison
equality, substitution, extensionality, uniqueness, and proof patterns
backend-independent set interfaces, set operations, set laws, and concrete set backends
typed and set-theoretic maps, relations and graphs, image/preimage/fibers, injective/surjective/bijective maps, inverses, restrictions, products, operations, and laws
arity, operation laws, identity elements, inverses, compatibility, distributivity, and divisibility
relation predicates, equivalence relations, partitions, quotient sets, and order relations
algebraic signatures, structures, models, homomorphisms, substructures, quotient structures, and universal properties

concepts.name: PublicSetOperations
concepts.role: names the backend-independent finite set-operation surface: set objects, elements, membership, empty set, singleton, pair, union, intersection, and subset

concepts.name: PublicSetOperationLaws
concepts.role: records the memberwise readings for the public operation names

concepts.name: SetInterface
concepts.role: the ordinary backend-independent set API used by generic set proofs

concepts.name: SetInterfaceLaws
concepts.role: extends the operation laws with extensionality so memberwise equivalence can prove set equality

concepts.name: GenericSetModel
concepts.role: bundles a concrete backend as an interface together with proofs of the interface laws

concepts.name: LRASet public adapter
concepts.role: exposes the current project predicate-set backend through the public set interface

usage: Import LRA.VolumeI.Set.Theory when writing ordinary set-theory theorems.
Take parameters (interface : SetInterface) and (laws : SetInterfaceLaws interface) instead of selecting a concrete backend.
State set objects using interface.SetObject and elements using interface.Element.
Use Empty, Singleton, Pair, Union, Intersection, and Subset from the public surface.
Use membership-reading theorems such as UnionMembership and IntersectionMembership to reduce set operations to elementwise logic.
Use SetExtensionality or SetExtensionalityIff when a goal is equality of generic sets.
Use SubsetMembership for subset goals and SetEqualityIffMutualSubset when equality is naturally proved by two inclusions.
Use BooleanSetOperations or IndexedSetOperations only when the theorem genuinely needs complement, difference, universal sets, or indexed unions/intersections.

recipes.title: Prove a generic set equality
recipes.text: Reduce equality to memberwise equivalence with SetExtensionality, then use the operation membership laws.

recipes.title: Prove a subset claim
recipes.text: Rewrite the subset statement with SubsetMembership and prove the resulting implication on an arbitrary element.

recipes.title: Use a concrete backend
recipes.text: Instantiate a concrete adapter such as publicOperations for LRASet, pass its law theorem, and then reuse the generic theorem without reproving it for that backend.
